sentences.text: ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant - original claimant, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and G.S.R.T.C vs Niruben Natwarlal Gandhi on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138897927/
1 award dated 28.02.2006 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court No.14, Vadodara, in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.725 NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2508/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined of 1993, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.3,95,000/- with 9% per annum interest to the claimant, holding the opponents i.e. owner, driver and insurance company liable, jointly and severally.
2.

Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,
the present appeal has been preferred by claimant - before this Court.

3. Heard learned advocate Mr. Devang Bhatt for learned advocate Mr. H.S. Munshaw for the appellant and learned advocate Mr. Surendra Patel for learned advocate Mr. Nilesh A. Pandya for the respondents.
4.

Mr. Bhatt has contended that the present appeal is filed mainly on two grounds on the aspect of negligence and also on the aspect of quantum as the income of deceased is considered on higher side and prospective income added for 50% instead of 40% as required in view of the judgment of Sarla Verma and Pranav Shethy, and therefore, he has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error and required interference from this Court.

5. Learned advocate Mr. Surendra Patel appearing for learned advocate Mr. Pandya supported the judgment of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2508/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined Tribunal and further submitted that the deceased was working in the Gulf country as a Watchman in Oman Police and as per the documentary evidence, he was earning Rs.9000/-.
However, the Tribunal has considered only Rs.8000/- per month, and thereafter, added 50% in the income and accordingly Rs.6000/- is considered as future prospect.
Ultimately, he has submitted that Rs.3,95,000/- has awarded with 9% interest.
The interest awarded by the Tribunal is also on higher side, and therefore, he prays to pass appropriate orders.

5.1 Learned advocate Mr. Surendra Patel has submitted that the Tribunal has considered the income of Rs.8000/- instead of Rs.9000/- which is required to be considered, and thereafter, also the Tribunal has committed an error in adding only Rs.4000/-, and thereafter, divided by 2, therefore,
instead of prospective income is required to be increased from Rs.8000/- to Rs.12,000/- which comes to Rs.6000/-.
The Tribunal has also committed an error in taking age of the mother for the consideration of the multiplier.
The mother aged 45 years, and therefore, the multiplier is given 15.
At the time of accident, deceased was aged 28 years 4 months old, and therefore, the multiplier should be 17.
There personal deduction and considering all the aspect, the Tribunal ought to have grant some more NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2508/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined compensation.

However, he has fairly submitted that he has not filed any cross objection,
and therefore, he is not stretching any further about the amount of compensation but he has submitted that the Tribunal has not granted sufficient compensation and has further submitted that
in view of the fact that the matters arising from the same accident, the present appellant has preferred First Appeal No.2509 of 2007, First Appeal No.2510 of 2007 and First Appeal No.2512 of 2007.
Those appeals are withdrawn by order dated 08.04.2008, and therefore, it is now not open for the present appellant to challenge the aspect of negligence.

He has further submitted otherwise G.S.R.T.C vs Niruben Natwarlal Gandhi on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138897927/
2

also from the reading of the judgment, the Tribunal has considered all relevant aspect regarding the negligence aspect as he face to ran into the road side pit with a view to avoid the accident and in turn with the collision with the bus.

The jeep ran into the road side pit otherwise also Panchnama and other documentary evidence are properly examined by the Tribunal, and therefore, the learned advocate for the respondent submits that no interference is called for.
6. I have considered the rival submissions.

The Court, while granting the compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act is required to be kept in mind principle of just compensation which should be arrived on the fair and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2508/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined reasonable appreciation of evidence.
In the accident cases strict proof is not required and the case of the claimant is required to be proved on the principal of preponderance of probability.

Now considering the submissions, it prima facie transpires from the record that by order dated 08.04.2008, the First Appeal arising from the same accident i.e. First Appeal No.2509 of 2007, First Appeal No.2510 of 2007 and First Appeal No.2512 of 2007 are withdrawn by the appellant.
Therefore, the challenge to the impugned judgment is dropped and the judgment has become final and the findings recorded in the judgment also become final to that extent.

Otherwise also, while perusing the findings on issue No.1, it transpires that the Tribunal has considered the time of incident, place of incident and deposition of the eye witness Nishaben Sureshkumar, who has seen the accident and also considered the Panchnama as well as other documentary evidence and has rightly come to the conclusion that the driver of the bus is negligent as he was driving bus in rash and negligent manner.

Now considering the aspect of quantum, the Tribunal has considered the quantum in very conservative manner as there is sufficient evidence available on record by way of the labour card issued from the Oman Government and copy of the Passport and Visa also indicates that deceased was serving in Oman.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2508/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined
He was getting salary of 175 Riyal which is equivalent to Rs.9000/- in the year 1993.

Thereafter, the Tribunal has considered the income could be Rs.4000/- and therefore, considered the income should be presumed as Rs.8000/- per month in currency equivalent to Indian Rupees, and thereafter, the Tribunal has applied multiplier on the basis of age of mother which ought to have been on the basis of age of the deceased, and therefore, instead of 15, 17 multiplier is required to be added.
The Tribunal has not awarded any proper amount towards the compensation as only Rs.5000/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and no amount towards the consortium is awarded.
Considering all this amount which is awarded by the Tribunal is Rs.3,95,000/- is on very lower side.
However, considering the fact that the appeal is preferred by the Gujarat State Transport Corporation and no cross objection or appeal is filed by the claimant.
Therefore, this Court, in peculiar facts and circumstances is not exercising the powers to enhance the amount which ought to have been enhanced in the facts of the present case.
Otherwise Court has power to even enhance the amount of compensation even in absence of any cross objection in any appropriate case.

7. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2508/2007 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/06/2024 undefined to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

Section 168 of the Motor G.S.R.T.C vs Niruben Natwarlal Gandhi on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138897927/
3 Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

8. Considering the above discussion, no interference is called for in the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Tribunal.
Accordingly, appeal requires to be dismissed and is hereby dismissed.
9. Record and Proceedings received by this Court shall sent forthwith to the concerned Tribunal within 2 weeks.
Amount lying before the Tribunal, if any, shall be disbursed to the claimant without any further delay by the Tribunal after due verification.

(SANDEEP N. BHATT,J) Manoj Kumar Rai G.S.R.T.C vs Niruben Natwarlal Gandhi on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138897927/
